title: Warp entropy and kernel ecosystem exploration
content:
Summary:

This note captures an exploratory profiling run that tries to tease apart anecdotally observed latency jitter we’ve been seeing on mixed-sequence workloads. The working name is 'warp entropy' — shorthand for the hypothesis that small variations in warp occupancy, register pressure, and micro-scheduling (handshake delays) change the kernel affinity decision and introduce bimodal latency in steady-state serving. We profiled a set of microbenchmarks across FlashAttention, paged-attention, and a couple fused-op variants to identify repeatable triggers and inexpensive indicator metrics we can collect in prod.

Goals:
- Produce a lightweight diagnostic (p99/p999 correlation) that signals when kernel-affinity flips are likely.
- Quantify the latency delta when FlashAttention vs paged-attn vs fusedops are chosen across realistic sequence mixes.
- Collect a small set of perf counters that are useful signals (e.g., warp occupancy estimate, issued_sch_stalls, register spill indications).

Background / Motivation:
We see reproducible 2x latency spikes in 99.9% tail inside Dedicated clusters running mixed short/long prompt mixes. Existing traces show different kernels being selected mid-episode; when that happens, latencies jump and KV cache behavior becomes bursty. Prior docs focused on fusion boundaries and prefetch hysteresis; here I try to connect that to low-level occupancy and scheduler-side heuristics.

Test environment:
- Platform: Dedicated cluster (p4d-like) on CIF-GPU-16 nodes (4xA100 equiv).
- Runtime: local dev branch: runtime/warmup/warp-probe (commit: 9f3be1e).
- Models: distilled-gpt-1.3B (toy) and llama-7B cutdown (weights quantized to int8 where applicable).
- Kernels: flash-v2, paged-v1, fused-io-v3 (custom fused-kernel build).
- Tooling: nsys (Nsight Systems), CUPTI counters extraction via our flame adaptor, perf for CPU-side, and lightweight in-runtime probes emitting JSON line stats at kernel decision points.

Synthetic workload design:
- Sequence mixes: (A) 90% short (8 tokens), 10% long (1024 tokens); (B) 50/50 short/long; (C) heavy long tails (25% long, 75% mids 128–512).
- Request interarrival patterns: Poisson lambda tuned to create small-batch steady-state (targeting avg batch size 6–10) and burst window simulations (spikes pushing burst to 24–32).
- Affinity seeds: we toggle the kernel selector thresholds to force more flash or more paged decisions in some runs so we can compare.

Commands / snippets used:
- workload runner: ./bin/warp_probe --model distilled-gpt --mix A --rate 120 --duration 600 --trace kernel-decisions.jsonl
- collect CUPTI: ./scripts/cupti_collect.sh --pid <servlet_pid> --counters "sm__warps_active.avg,sm__inst_executed.avg,sm__stall_barrier.avg,sm__pipe_tensor_cycles.active"
- nsys capture: nsys profile --output=warpA --trace=cuda,osrt --stop-on-exit -- ./bin/warp_probe ...

Representative findings (short form):
1) Bimodal p99 in mix A when batch coalescer output occasionally produces 1 vs 2 micro-batches hitting the kernel scheduler. The difference maps to ~6–9ms vs ~14–20ms for a single token decode step on 7B quant model.
2) When warp occupancy estimate (sm__warps_active.avg scaled per-SM) drops below an empirical threshold (~28% on our nodes), selector prefers paged-attn fallback; that choice is correlated with higher register spills on fusedops attempts (observed via increase in local memory traffic).
3) Paged-attn shows more consistent per-step latency under sustained high sequence length, but has higher steady-state cost and variance increases when many small requests coalesce. FlashAttention excels at small-batch throughput but suffers tail jumps when micro-scheduler adds dequeue jitter.
4) Fusedops (io-v3) can win when register pressure stays below threshold; a second-order interaction between sequence alignment (pad to power-of-two) and kernel tile size causes occasional extra bank conflicts.

Example extracted metrics timeline (simplified):
- t=120s: burst window, avg batch = 10 -> sm__warps_active.avg = 0.43 -> flash selected -> step latency p50 ~ 7.3ms
- t=121s: coalescer produced uneven split (batches 4 + 6) -> sm__warps_active.avg = 0.27 -> selector flipped -> paged selected -> step latency p50 ~ 13.8ms
- CPU-side: small GC spike earlier correlated with 200us delay in enqueue path (non-deterministic) that nudges kernel handshake timing.

Hypotheses / causal chain (working):
- Micro-enqueue jitter (CPU syscall/GC/preemption) changes handoff boundary between runtime and scheduler by a few 100s of microseconds.
- That jitter changes instantaneous batch population and per-SM warp occupancy estimate used by runtime's kernel selector heuristics.
- Selector heuristics choose between flash / paged / fused; some kernel choices are sensitive to register pressure and bank conflicts leading to sudden latency jumps.

Quick wins and low-risk changes to test:
- Emit lightweight occupancy delta metric at every decision point (already instrumented in probe branch). Add that as a trace field in prod; compute a rolling correlation with tail latency.
- Slightly bias selector to prefer Flash when occupancy sits in the ambiguous range (0.25–0.35) and enable a short backoff if a flip happens (avoid oscillation).
- Tune coalescer to avoid producing micro-splits below a batch-size floor of 6 unless under-utilized.
- Add a cheap early registry check: if register pressure metric estimate (from a prior kernel run) > threshold, avoid fusedops optimistic path.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How stable is sm__warps_active.avg across different GPU types (A100 vs H100)? Our threshold might need to be device-specific. Run quick calibration on H100 testbeds.
- Can we get a reliable, low-overhead estimate of expected register spills from the kernel metadata instead of relying purely on dynamic perf counters?
- Is there a simpler CPU-side signal (enqueue latency quantile) that lets us pre-emptively adjust coalescer behavior before kernel flip occurs?
- Investigate whether NVLink traffic patterns correlate with the same flips (we saw hints in one capture where nvlink congestion preceded a paged fallback).

Action items (small tracked tasks):
- [Priya] Wire the occupancy delta field into the hosted trace schema and push to flame adaptor (ETA: 2024-11-15).
- [Evan] Run the same warp-probe suite on H100 staging and post summarized counters (ETA: 2024-11-18).
- [Marisol] Prototype selector bias toggle and run A/B on a subset of Dedicated instances (ETA: 2024-11-22).
- [Samir] Check whether coalescer floor of 6 affects throughput in low-utilization windows; prepare regression plan (ETA: 2024-11-20).

Notes to self / informal observations:
- The 'entropy' analogy seems useful for communicating to SRE/product — it's about small, chaotic changes at the micro-scheduling layer, not about model quality. Keep the naming lightweight.
- Collected a couple of noisy nsight captures; storing them in GS bucket gs://redwood-dev/warp-raw/ — big files (100s MB).
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime thread titled "warp-entropy probe" has preliminary charts; link in PR.

Appendix: raw sample detector log (one line, JSONL)
{"ts":1700000123.234, "model":"llama-7B", "mix":"A", "decision":"flash", "sm_warps_active":0.431, "batch_sz":10, "step_latency_ms":7.31}

End of note. This is exploratory; append additional capture IDs as runs complete.

-- Priya K.
